fields.mechanism: Guide clearance in the flat-faced follower linkage induces impact and friction forces that drive non-linear dynamic motion of the follower stem.
fields.intervention: Reduce or eliminate the clearance between the 16 mm flat-faced cam follower stem and its guide bore on the fixed stud to the minimum value identified by the paper's non-linear dynamic analysis as suppressing chaotic response, thereby eliminating the impact loads that initiate rolling-contact fatigue spalling without altering the cam profile, follower diameter class, cycle rate, or maintenance interval.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of clearance-induced impact forces stabilizes the follower kinematics, preventing the transient contact stress peaks that cause surface fatigue spalling within 6 to 9 weeks, maintaining continuous operation at 420 cycles per minute without food-contact metal debris contamination.
fields.falsification_test: Operate the folding station at 420 cycles per minute with the guide clearance reduced to the simulation-optimized value; inspect the 16 mm flat-faced follower contact face for spalling after 10 weeks of 20-hour-per-day service — if spalling or metal debris is present, the intervention fails.
fields.mechanism_source_span: The system has clearances between the flat-faced follower and the guides and the effect of clearance is analyzed.

fields.mechanism: Clearance between the flat-faced follower and its guides induces non-linear impact dynamics that govern follower motion and loading.
fields.intervention: Invert the active clearance effect by passively preloading the follower guide to eliminate clearance, using the measured largest Lyapunov exponent as a deterministic tuning target to suppress chaotic impact forces at 420 cycles per minute without altering the cam profile or the 16 mm follower diameter class.

fields.mechanism: Non-linear dynamic impact forces between the flat-faced follower and its guides caused by clearance, generating transient contact stress peaks that drive rolling-contact fatigue spalling.
fields.intervention: Apply a multi-physics hybrid intervention combining mechanical and thermal domains: use the non-linear dynamic simulation method from the paper to quantify exact guide clearances via high-resolution optical marker measurement on the follower stem, then install thermally matched composite guide bushings with zero-clearance interference fit at operating temperature. The thermal expansion of the composite material under 20-hour continuous running closes the clearance dynamically, eliminating the impact phenomenon described in the paper without altering the cam profile or the 16 mm follower diameter class.
fields.expected_effect: Elimination of the impact-induced transient Hertzian stress spikes between the flat-faced follower and guides suppresses subsurface shear stress accumulation, preventing surface fatigue spalling beyond the 9-week failure window and stopping metal debris contamination of food-contact surfaces while maintaining 420 cycles per minute.
fields.falsification_test: Mount a high-resolution optical marker on the follower stem as described in the paper and measure y-direction displacement amplitude during operation at 420 cycles per minute; if peak-to-peak displacement exceeds 5 micrometers after thermal stabilization, or if the largest Lyapunov exponent indicates chaotic motion, the clearance elimination has failed. Inspect followers weekly for 12 weeks; any visible spalling falsifies the intervention.
